2027-06-06.title: Third Sunday after Pentecost
readings: The Twelve sent out two by two
We will not worship the golden statue
Through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed
I am the bread of life
2027-06-06.verse: I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
theo: Jesus says: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty… Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away… This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.” And: “No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father who sent me.” Faith itself is a gift: the Father draws, the Spirit moves the heart.

In the evening Gospel Jesus is rejected in his own town: “Prophets are not without honor, except in their hometown, and among their own kin, and in their own house.” Yet he does not stop. He sends the Twelve two by two, with authority over unclean spirits. “So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.” The mission of the Church begins in weakness and is carried by the Spirit's power.

In the book of Daniel three young men stand before a golden statue and a blazing furnace. They say to the king: “If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.” This is faith that does not bargain: God first, whatever happens.

St Paul writes: “So then, whenever we have an opportunity, let us work for the good of all, and especially for those of the family of faith… May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ… a new creation is everything!” In Baptism we became a new creation; the bread of life keeps us alive as God's new people.
conn: Genesis 42: the brothers recognise their guilt; Jeremiah 3: “Return to me”; Acts 13:38: forgiveness proclaimed through Jesus.
Daniel 3: fidelity under threat; Galatians 6:14: boasting only in the Cross.
Mark 6:13: the apostles anoint the sick; the Church sees here a hint of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick (James 5:14).
Joseph gives grain to his hungry brothers (Genesis 42:25); Jesus is the bread of life for the world.
altar: “I am the bread of life.” At the Holy Qurbono the Father draws us to the Son, and the Son gives himself to us, so that we may never hunger and may be raised on the last day.
outline: Rejected at home, yet sending others.
Come to Jesus; he will never drive you away.
Mission in weakness: repentance, healing, anointing.
The three young men: faith without bargaining.
Doing good to all, boasting only in the Cross.
“Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.”
live: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with a family member or friend.
Tell God: “Even if you do not answer as I wish, I will trust you.”
Prepare for Holy Qurbono with confession if needed.
fathers: “No one comes unless drawn.” You are drawn not by force but by delight; show a green branch to a sheep and you draw it; so Christ, revealed by the Father, draws us (Tractates on John 26, 4–5).
The three youths teach us that the faithful must prefer death to denying God, and God stood with them in the furnace (Commentary on Daniel II).
magis: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven; whoever eats of this bread will live for ever.”
The Church believes that a special sacrament for the sick was instituted by Christ, hinted at in Mark 6:13 and promulgated by James 5:14.
Faith requires us to worship God alone and refuse all idols.
saints: 8 June: St Mariam Thresia. 11 June: Mar Barthulmai (Bartholomew) and Mar Barnabas, Apostles; anniversary of the erection of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy (11 June 1932). 13 June: St Antony of Padua.
2027-06-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, bread of life, draw us to yourself and never drive us away. Make us faithful like the three young men in the furnace, send us two by two to heal and proclaim repentance, and make us a new creation for the good of all. Amen.

quick: “I am the bread of life”: whoever comes to Jesus will never hunger.
The Twelve are sent two by two to preach repentance and heal.
“But if not”: faith that will not worship idols whatever happens.
2027-06-06.action: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with someone from your family.
2027-06-06.question: Do I trust God even when he does not answer as I want?
2027-06-06.special: Third Sunday after Pentecost. This week (11 June): anniversary of the erection of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Hierarchy in 1932.
illus: In 1930 Mar Ivanios and a few companions entered communion with the Catholic Church, leaving buildings and properties behind. They had little, but went out like the apostles, two by two. In 1932 the Syro-Malankara hierarchy was erected. Faith first, whatever it costs.

family.explain: Three young men would not bow down to a golden statue, even when the king threatened them with fire. They loved God more than anything!
family.intention: We pray for courage to put God first always.
family.ask: Ask: “What ‘golden statues’ tempt us to put them before God?”

kidsaint: A Franciscan priest who preached so well that people said even the fish came to listen! He loved the poor, and people still give “St Antony's bread” to the hungry. Lesson: share your bread as Jesus shares himself.
term: Jesus sent the apostles in pairs (Mark 6:7; Luke 10:1): for support, for witness (two witnesses make a testimony), and as a sign that mission is done in communion, not alone.
termMore: On 11 June 1932 Pope Pius XI, by the bull Christo Pastorum Principi, erected the Syro-Malankara hierarchy with the Archeparchy of Trivandrum and the Eparchy of Tiruvalla. In 2005 the Church was raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus went to his own town and was rejected. “Prophets are not without honor, except in their hometown.” Did he give up? No. He called the Twelve and sent them out two by two. They preached repentance, cast out demons, and anointed the sick with oil. The mission of the Church began with rejection, and went on in the power of God.

In the Gospel of John Jesus says: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry… anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.” What a promise! No sinner who comes to him is turned away. And he says: “No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father.” If you are here today, the Father has drawn you.

In the book of Daniel three young men refuse to worship the golden statue. They say: our God can save us from the fire; “but if not,” we still will not worship your gods. This is mature faith. It does not say “God, if you give me this, I will believe.” It says “God, whatever happens, I belong to you.” Our Malankara Church, born in 1930 with Mar Ivanios, knows this faith: they left property and buildings, but kept communion.

St Paul says: let us do good to all, and boast only in the Cross; what matters is a new creation. This week, go two by two: visit a sick or lonely person with someone from your family. And come often to the bread of life. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent his friends out two by two, like partners, to tell people about God and to help sick people.
In the Bible, three brave young men would not bow to a golden statue, even when the king was angry. They loved God more than anything!
Jesus says: “I am the bread of life.” Who can you visit this week with your mum, dad or friend?

intro: Theme: “Sent two by two, fed by the Bread of Life.”
Rejected in his hometown, Jesus does not stop; he sends the Twelve two by two. In John he says: “I am the bread of life.” The three young men in Daniel show the courage of faith that refuses idols.

points.h: Come to the Bread of Life
sub: Isaiah invites the thirsty and the poor to come and eat freely.
Jesus says: whoever comes to me will never hunger; I will never drive away anyone who comes.
In the Holy Qurbono that invitation is fulfilled.
q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat!
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.”
points.apply: Prepare well for your next Holy Communion with a few minutes of silent prayer.

sub: “Two are better than one”: mission is done in communion, not alone.
Jesus sends the Twelve with authority; they preach repentance, cast out demons and anoint the sick.
The Church sees here a hint of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
q: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up the other.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.
points.apply: Visit a sick or lonely person this week with a family member or friend.

points.h: Faith that will not bow to idols
sub: The three young men: “Our God is able to deliver us … but if not, we will not serve your gods.”
Mature faith does not bargain with God.
St Paul boasts only in the Cross, and in being a new creation.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire … let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
points.apply: Name one modern “golden statue” (money, status, screens) and refuse to bow to it this week.

concl: Fed by Christ, sent together, faithful to the end: this is the Church after Pentecost.
Let us come to the Bread of Life and go out to share it.
2027-06-06.resolve: Pray for the Syro-Malankara Church on the anniversary of its hierarchy (11 June 1932).
